name: anschreiben-pilot
what: AI cover-letter generator for the DACH market, forked from vincanger/coverlettergpt (GPL-3.0). Differentiation: correct German (DIN 5008) formatting, deliberately simpler than the 11 competitors found (JobStep, Rezi, MakeMyCV, bewerbung.net, bewerbung2go.de, LiveCareer, Jotform, onlinelebenslauf.com, ki-motivationsschreiben.ch, jobs.ch, Bewerbung.ai), plus a free Bewerbungsmappe PDF-merger as a growth hook. Full research and spec live in brain: brain/projects/micro-saas-dach.md and brain/projects/micro-saas-dach-spec-cover-letter-cv.md.

Found and fixed a CRITICAL payment security hole (2026-09-23), after Saskia asked whether vince's original payment code had actually been checked: the Stripe webhook had NO signature verification at all — anyone could POST a forged 'checkout.session.completed' straight to /stripe-webhook naming any Stripe customer ID and the code would grant hasPaid=true for free, no payment needed. Fixed with Wasp's middlewareConfigFn (swaps JSON parsing for raw body parsing on that one route) + stripe.webhooks.constructEvent. Verified by actually forging requests against the running server: no signature (400), garbage signature (400), wrong-secret signature (400), then a correctly HMAC-signed payload (200) — both the fail and success paths proven, not assumed.

Added rate limiting (10/hour + 50/day per user, tightened from an initial 20/hour after Saskia questioned whether that was reasonable) and input length caps to every OpenAI-calling action — previously a paying user had no limit at all on generations, a real cost-abuse gap on the GPT-4o tier specifically.
